memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Instead, I give to the Levites as their inheritance the tithes that the Israelites present as an offering to the Lord. That is why I said concerning them: 'They will have no inheritance among the Israelites.'" Then the Lord spoke to Moses: "Speak to the Levites and say to them: 'When you receive from the Israelites the tithe I give you as your inheritance, you must present a tenth of that tithe as the Lord's offering.'" — Num 18:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a lovely detail that is easy to miss. The Levites received the tithes of the people as their provision — but then they too were to give a tithe of what they received back to the Lord. Even those who lived off the offerings were called to be givers themselves. No one was exempt from the joy and discipline of giving to God.

This is a gentle challenge to any of us who might think giving is only for those with plenty. The Levites owned no land and lived on what others provided, yet they still gave. Giving was not about how much they had, but about honouring God with whatever they received. Everyone, however modest their means, was invited to give back to the Lord.

There is deep wisdom in this. Giving is not primarily about God needing our resources; He owns everything already. It is about the posture of our hearts. When even those living on gifts give in return, it declares that everything ultimately belongs to God and flows back to Him. Giving keeps our hearts from clutching, reminding us that we are stewards, not owners.

The pattern flows from grace. We give because we have first received. Everything we have has come from God's hand, and giving is simply returning a portion to the One who gave it all. This finds its fullest meaning in Christ, who, though rich, became poor for our sake, so that we might become rich. Having received such a gift, how can we not become generous givers ourselves? Whatever your means, you are invited into the grace of giving.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you think of giving as only for those with plenty?
2. How does giving guard your heart from clutching what you have?
3. How does receiving grace in Christ make you a generous giver?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that everything I have flows from Your hand. Teach me the grace of giving, whatever my means, holding all things loosely as Your steward. Thank You for Christ, who became poor to make me rich. Amen.
